clauses.reason: The first sentence provides that Executive Order No. 9635 and Executive Order No. 9904 “are hereby revoked”. The order states no effective date, so the revocation took effect when signed on April 20, 1950 (the filing stamp reads April 20, 1950 as well). The command was exhausted by performance on that date and the end source is the order's own text.

The second sentence says the revocation made by this order shall not be construed as reviving Executive Order No. 8984 and Executive Order No. 9096 (as amended), which Executive Order No. 9635 had revoked. It limits only the effect of the revocation performed in the first sentence, so it operated once, when that revocation took effect on April 20, 1950, and has no separate continuing command. Its consequence, that the two named earlier orders were not revived, is disclosed as a surviving effect and is not claimed as an operative command.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 10123 (15 FR 2265 (Federal Register of April 22, 1950)) was signed April 20, 1950. The filing stamp printed after the order reads April 20, 1950; the held OCR prints the signing line as April 2d, 1950, which is the register's signing date of April 20, 1950 read through an OCR error. Its held Federal Register text, registered as the original representation for this order, prints the order number, its title and the signing date, and its operative command is the sentence providing that Executive Order No. 9635 and Executive Order No. 9904, which amended it, “are hereby revoked”, followed by a sentence limiting the effect of the revocation. On 2026-10-14 the command is terminated: a revoking command is complete when it takes effect, and this order states no separate effective date, so it took effect when signed on April 20, 1950. The order contains no condition, postponement, report, transfer or continuing duty. No other held text cites this order's number by an order citation. The Federal Register disposition-note search, the U.S. Code citation search and the eCFR citation search each report no hit naming this order; the last two test only for current citations and are cited as bounded searches. The surviving consequence is that Executive Order No. 9635 of September 29, 1945 (organization of the Navy Department and the Naval Establishment) and Executive Order No. 9904 of November 13, 1947, which amended it remains revoked; that consequence follows from the performed command and is not a command that still has to end.
